title: Public Health Digital Communication Fellowship: Six-Month Fellowship for Health Experts, Researchers, Clinicians and Policy Leaders
summary: Public health information plays an increasingly important role in how people understand their health, make decisions, access healthcare services, and respond to health-related issues. However, having strong expertise in public health, medicine, research, or health policy does not automatically mean that this expertise is reaching the public in a clear, engaging, and accessible way. A new six-month fellowship for health experts, researchers, clinicians, policy leaders, and evidence-based communicators offers an opportunity for professionals who want to turn their public health expertise into stronger public-facing communication and build a more effective digital presence. The fellowship is designed for individuals who already have expertise in health-related fields and want to learn how to communicate accurate and credible information effectively in today s digital environment. Participants will work alongside established digital communicators to develop accurate and engaging content that reflects how people discover, understand, and act on health information today. About the Public Health Digital Communication Fellowship The fellowship is a six-month professional development opportunity focused on the intersection of public health expertise and digital communication. Rather than focusing only on developing technical knowledge in public health, the fellowship emphasizes the ability to translate existing expertise into content that can be understood and used by the public. This distinction is particularly important in today s digital environment, where people increasingly encounter health information through online platforms. Health experts may have extensive knowledge, research findings, clinical experience, or policy expertise, but communicating that information effectively requires additional skills. The fellowship is therefore intended to help participants bridge the gap between: Public health expertise → Digital communication → Public understanding → Informed action Through collaboration with established digital communicators, fellows will have the opportunity to develop content that is both accurate and engaging , while considering how people search for, consume, understand, and respond to health information online. Why Public Health Communication Matters Public health information can be complex. Research papers, clinical evidence, health policies, epidemiological data, and technical recommendations are often written for professional audiences. However, members of the public may need to understand the same information in much simpler and more practical terms. Effective public health communication helps make complex information more accessible. For example, a health professional may understand a research finding in technical detail, while a member of the public may need to know: What does this information mean? Does it affect me? What should I do? Where can I find reliable information? How can I distinguish evidence from misinformation? What action should I take based on the available evidence? The fellowship s focus on creating accurate, engaging digital content is designed around this challenge. What the Fellowship Focuses On The central objective is to help health professionals and experts develop a stronger public-facing digital presence . This means participants will work on communicating their expertise beyond traditional professional or academic audiences. The fellowship brings together two important areas: 1. Public Health Expertise Participants are expected to bring existing knowledge and expertise from areas such as: Public health Clinical practice Health research Health policy Evidence-based communication Other relevant health-related fields 2. Digital Communication Participants will work alongside established digital communicators to develop content that is suitable for today s digital information environment. This involves thinking about how audiences: Find health information. Understand health information. Engage with health content. Decide whether information is credible. Use information to make health-related decisions. The combination allows participants to transform their existing expertise into communication that can reach broader audiences. Who Is the Fellowship Designed For? The fellowship specifically identifies several groups of professionals who may benefit from the opportunity. Health Experts Health experts with established knowledge in public health or related areas can use the fellowship to improve how they communicate their expertise to wider audiences. Researchers Researchers who produce evidence and scientific findings may benefit from learning how to translate complex research into accessible public-facing content. This can help researchers communicate findings beyond academic publications and professional conferences. Clinicians Clinicians possess valuable practical knowledge based on their professional experience and interaction with patients. The fellowship can support clinicians who want to develop a stronger digital presence and communicate evidence-based health information to wider audiences. Policy Leaders Health policy leaders can use effective digital communication to explain policies, evidence, and public health issues in ways that are more accessible to non-specialist audiences. Evidence-Based Communicators The opportunity also specifically welcomes individuals working in evidence-based communication. For these professionals, the fellowship provides an opportunity to further develop their ability to communicate credible health information through digital channels. Building a Stronger Public-Facing Digital Presence One of the central goals of the fellowship is helping participants establish or strengthen their public-facing digital presence . A digital presence allows professionals to communicate directly with audiences outside traditional professional settings. For health experts, this can mean creating content that makes their expertise easier to discover and understand. Instead of limiting communication to: Academic papers Professional conferences Technical reports Institutional publications Specialist audiences participants can explore ways to communicate health information through digital content designed for broader audiences. The fellowship therefore focuses on helping professionals take their expertise and make it more accessible in the environments where people increasingly search for information. Working With Established Digital Communicators An important feature of the fellowship is the opportunity to work alongside established digital communicators . This provides participants with exposure to professionals who understand how digital audiences consume information. The collaboration can help bridge the gap between knowing health information and knowing how to communicate that information effectively online. Participants will be able to work in an environment where health expertise and digital communication come together. The focus is not simply on producing more content. It is on developing content that is: Accurate Evidence-based Engaging Accessible Relevant to public audiences Creating Accurate Health Content Accuracy is particularly important when communicating health information. Health misinformation can create confusion and make it difficult for people to distinguish credible information from unsupported claims. The fellowship specifically emphasizes the creation of accurate content . This means that participants existing health expertise can serve as the foundation for developing trustworthy public-facing communication. For researchers and clinicians, this may provide an opportunity to communicate evidence in formats that are easier for non-specialists to understand. For policy leaders and health communicators, it can provide a framework for explaining complex health topics to broader audiences. Creating Engaging Health Content Accuracy alone does not necessarily guarantee that people will read, understand, or engage with health information. Digital audiences are exposed to large amounts of information every day. As a result, health information also needs to be presented in ways that capture attention and encourage understanding. The fellowship therefore combines accuracy with engagement . This means participants will be working toward content that communicates evidence without unnecessarily losing the audience s attention. The goal is to make health information easier for people to discover, understand, and use. Understanding How People Find Health Information The fellowship is designed around the realities of modern digital information consumption. People increasingly search online when they want answers to health-related questions. The way people discover information can therefore influence which health messages they encounter. Understanding how people find health information is an important part of developing an effective digital communication strategy. Professionals participating in the fellowship can use this perspective to think more strategically about how their expertise is presented and made accessible to audiences. Helping People Understand Health Information Finding health information is only the first step. People also need to understand what the information means. Technical terminology and highly specialized explanations can make health information difficult for non-specialist audiences to interpret. The fellowship focuses on developing content that is engaging and accessible while maintaining accuracy. This can help health professionals communicate complex ideas in ways that are easier for broader audiences to understand. Supporting Informed Action The fellowship description also highlights how people act on health information . This means the communication process extends beyond simply publishing information. Effective health communication should consider what audiences do after encountering a health message. The fellowship therefore brings together three stages of the digital health-information journey: Finding health information. Understanding health information. Acting on health information. This approach positions digital communication as an important part of public health engagement. Potential Benefits of the Fellowship Participants can potentially gain several professional benefits from taking part in the six-month fellowship. Strengthen Digital Communication Skills Participants can develop their ability to communicate health expertise in digital formats designed for public audiences. Build a Public-Facing Professional Profile The fellowship is specifically intended for professionals who want to build a stronger public-facing digital presence. Learn From Established Communicators Working alongside established digital communicators provides an opportunity to gain practical exposure to digital communication approaches. Translate Expertise Into Accessible Content Participants can learn to transform specialized knowledge into content that broader audiences can understand. Improve Public Engagement Developing accurate and engaging content can help health professionals communicate more effectively with people outside traditional professional settings. Expand the Reach of Health Expertise A stronger digital presence can help health experts make their knowledge more discoverable to audiences looking for reliable health information. Why This Opportunity May Be Relevant to Health Professionals Many health professionals have substantial expertise but limited opportunities to develop public-facing communication skills. A researcher may be highly experienced in conducting studies but less experienced in communicating findings through digital platforms. A clinician may have extensive patient-care experience but may not have developed a structured online communication strategy. A policy leader may understand complex health systems and policies but may need additional tools for explaining them to the public. This fellowship addresses that gap by bringing health expertise together with digital communication expertise. Six-Month Fellowship Structure The opportunity is described as a six-month fellowship . The six-month duration provides participants with an extended period in which to develop their public-facing communication capabilities rather than treating digital communication as a one-time workshop or short training. The fellowship s collaborative model involves working alongside established digital communicators throughout this period. However, the announcement provided does not specify the exact monthly schedule, number of participants, training format, meeting frequency, or individual fellowship activities. Therefore, prospective applicants should consult the official fellowship announcement or application materials for those details when available. Who Can Benefit From the Opportunity? The fellowship may be particularly relevant to professionals who already have a strong foundation in health-related knowledge and now want to become stronger communicators. It may be suitable for individuals who want to: Develop a professional digital identity. Communicate research findings to wider audiences. Explain health issues in accessible language. Increase the visibility of evidence-based health information. Develop engaging health content. Connect with digital communication professionals. Strengthen public engagement with their expertise. Application Deadline No application deadline is provided in the information supplied for this opportunity. Applicants should check the official fellowship announcement or application page for the deadline and application timeline before applying. Application Information The information provided describes the fellowship and its intended audience, but it does not include specific application instructions. The supplied announcement does not state: The application opening date. The application deadline. The application website. Required application documents. Selection criteria. Number of fellows selected. Fellowship stipend or financial support. Location or residency requirements. Whether participation is online, in person, or hybrid. These details should be verified through the official fellowship source before publication or application. APPLY HERE Conclusion The six-month Public Health Digital Communication Fellowship is designed for health professionals and experts who want to turn their knowledge into public-facing communication that is accurate, engaging, and relevant to the way people consume health information today. By bringing together health experts, researchers, clinicians, policy leaders, and evidence-based communicators with established digital communicators, the fellowship focuses on an increasingly important skill: communicating credible health expertise effectively in the digital environment. Participants will have the opportunity to work on developing content that considers how people find, understand, and act on health information , while also building a stronger public-facing digital presence. For professionals who already possess health expertise but want to expand their ability to communicate with wider audiences, this six-month fellowship represents an opportunity to connect subject-matter expertise with modern digital communication. Prospective applicants should review the official fellowship information carefully for application requirements, eligibility details, funding information, geographic restrictions, and the application deadline, as these details are not included in the announcement provided here. title: EvalYouth Asia 2026 Core Group: Call for Applications for Young and Emerging Evaluators
summary: EvalYouth Asia (EYA) has opened applications for its 2026 Core Group , inviting passionate young and emerging evaluators to take an active leadership role in strengthening evaluation practice, youth leadership, networking, and collaboration across the Asia-Pacific region. This is a volunteer leadership opportunity for individuals who are passionate about evaluation and evidence-informed decision-making and who want to contribute to a regional network supporting the next generation of evaluation professionals. Selected Core Group members will have the opportunity to contribute to strategic planning, develop initiatives for young and emerging evaluators, strengthen national and regional networks, build partnerships, and help shape the future direction of EvalYouth Asia. About EvalYouth Asia EvalYouth Asia is a regional platform that works to strengthen the participation and leadership of young and emerging evaluators (YEEs) within the evaluation community across Asia and the Pacific. Established in 2019 , EvalYouth Asia has focused on creating opportunities for young and emerging evaluators to connect with one another, develop their professional capacities, exchange knowledge, and participate meaningfully in the wider evaluation community. The network is driven by volunteers who contribute their time, expertise, and ideas to create a stronger and more connected community of emerging evaluation professionals. Through its activities, EvalYouth Asia seeks to provide young evaluators with opportunities to: Build professional networks across the Asia-Pacific region. Exchange knowledge and experiences in evaluation. Develop their leadership and professional skills. Participate in regional and global evaluation discussions. Engage with evaluation associations and other professional organizations. Strengthen youth participation in the evaluation field. Contribute to the development of the next generation of evaluation leaders. For 2026, EvalYouth Asia is seeking new Core Group members who can contribute their skills, perspectives, leadership, and commitment to the continued development of the regional network. What Is the EvalYouth Asia 2026 Core Group? The Core Group is a volunteer leadership group responsible for helping guide and implement the activities of EvalYouth Asia. Joining the Core Group is more than simply becoming a member of a professional network. Successful applicants will be expected to actively participate in planning, decision-making, community engagement, partnerships, and the development of initiatives benefiting young and emerging evaluators across the region. Core Group members will work collaboratively with other volunteers and regional partners to help strengthen the evaluation community and create opportunities for young professionals. Key Responsibilities of Core Group Members Selected members will contribute to a range of strategic, programmatic, networking, and community-building activities. 1. Provide Strategic Leadership Core Group members will help provide strategic leadership for the EvalYouth Asia network. This includes contributing ideas, participating in discussions about the network s direction, and helping identify activities and initiatives that can strengthen opportunities for young and emerging evaluators throughout the Asia-Pacific region. Members will therefore have an opportunity to contribute not only to individual activities but also to the broader development and direction of the regional network. 2. Design and Implement Regional Initiatives Core Group members will help design and implement initiatives that support young and emerging evaluators. These initiatives may contribute to areas such as: Professional development. Capacity building. Knowledge exchange. Networking. Youth leadership. Engagement within the evaluation community. Collaboration between young evaluators and established evaluation organizations. Members will be able to contribute their own ideas and expertise while working collaboratively with other members of the Core Group. 3. Strengthen National and Regional EvalYouth Networks Another important responsibility will be supporting the development and strengthening of EvalYouth networks at both the national and regional levels. Core Group members will work to encourage collaboration among existing networks and support efforts to establish new country chapters where appropriate. This provides an opportunity for individuals interested in regional network development and youth-led professional communities to contribute to a broader evaluation movement. 4. Build Partnerships With Key Stakeholders Core Group members will also contribute to partnership-building efforts. They will work to establish and strengthen relationships with: Evaluation associations. Development organizations. Professional evaluation networks. Other relevant stakeholders. Regional and international partners. The objective is to expand opportunities for youth engagement and create stronger connections between young and emerging evaluators and the wider evaluation ecosystem. 5. Collaborate With Regional Evaluation Organizations The Core Group will work closely with organizations and networks involved in evaluation across the region. This includes collaboration with the Asia Pacific Evaluation Association (APEA) , Voluntary Organizations for Professional Evaluation (VOPEs) , and other regional partners. Such collaboration can help create stronger links between young and emerging evaluators and established evaluation institutions and professional networks. 6. Participate in Monthly Core Group Meetings Core Group members are expected to participate in monthly Core Group meetings . These meetings provide an important space for members to: Discuss ongoing activities. Plan future initiatives. Make decisions. Coordinate responsibilities. Share updates. Discuss challenges and opportunities. Contribute ideas for strengthening the network. Applicants should therefore be prepared to maintain an ongoing commitment throughout their term. 7. Engage With EvalYouth Asia Members Core Group members will also be expected to regularly engage with the wider EvalYouth Asia community. This includes supporting community-building activities and helping maintain an active, connected, and collaborative network of young and emerging evaluators across the region. Community engagement is an important part of the role because the Core Group s activities are intended to respond to the needs and interests of the wider EvalYouth Asia membership. Volunteer Commitment The EvalYouth Asia Core Group is a voluntary leadership opportunity . Selected members are expected to dedicate approximately 20 hours per month to Core Group responsibilities. This means applicants should carefully consider whether they have sufficient time and availability to make a meaningful contribution alongside their existing academic, professional, or other commitments. In addition to the regular monthly commitment, each Core Group member is expected to lead or co-lead at least one major EvalYouth Asia initiative or workstream during their term . This requirement emphasizes the active leadership component of the opportunity. Applicants should therefore be prepared not only to attend meetings but also to take responsibility for delivering a substantial initiative or area of work. Who Should Apply? EvalYouth Asia is looking for young and emerging evaluators across the Asia-Pacific region who are interested in contributing to the development of evaluation practice and youth leadership. The opportunity is particularly relevant to individuals who demonstrate the following qualities: Passion for Evaluation Applicants should have a genuine interest in evaluation and evidence-informed decision-making . An interest in understanding what works, generating and using evidence, improving programs, and supporting better decision-making can be particularly relevant to the role. Commitment to the Evaluation Community Applicants should be committed to strengthening the evaluation community within the Asia-Pacific region. This includes an interest in supporting other young and emerging evaluators and contributing to a stronger regional evaluation ecosystem. Collaborative Approach Core Group work involves collaboration with other volunteers, evaluation organizations, development organizations, and regional and international partners. Applicants should therefore be comfortable working with others and contributing constructively to collaborative initiatives. Proactive and Willing to Contribute The role requires active participation rather than passive membership. Applicants should be willing to contribute their: Time. Skills. Knowledge. Ideas. Professional experience. Leadership. The expected commitment of approximately 20 hours per month makes availability and willingness to contribute important considerations. Interest in Regional and International Collaboration Applicants should be interested in working with diverse partners across the Asia-Pacific region and potentially engaging with regional and international organizations connected to evaluation and development. Why Join the EvalYouth Asia Core Group? Becoming part of the Core Group can provide an opportunity to contribute to the development of a regional professional community while gaining practical experience in leadership, collaboration, networking, and initiative management. Key areas of potential professional development include: Regional Networking Members can engage with young and emerging evaluators and evaluation stakeholders across the Asia-Pacific region. Leadership Experience Core Group members will participate in strategic decision-making and are expected to lead or co-lead a major initiative or workstream. Program and Initiative Development Members can gain practical experience in designing and implementing activities intended to support young evaluators. Partnership Building Working with evaluation associations, development organizations, VOPEs, APEA, and other partners can provide exposure to regional professional networks. Knowledge Exchange The network provides a platform for sharing ideas, experiences, and knowledge related to evaluation. Youth Leadership in Evaluation The Core Group provides an avenue for young and emerging evaluators to contribute directly to the development of the evaluation community and strengthen youth leadership within the field. Geographic Scope of the Opportunity The Core Group opportunity is intended for young and emerging evaluators across the Asia-Pacific region . The announcement does not provide a specific list of eligible countries. Therefore, applicants should interpret the geographic eligibility according to EvalYouth Asia s definition and scope of the Asia-Pacific region and confirm any country-specific requirements through the official application information. There is also no race, ethnicity, or racial-group restriction stated in the announcement . Application Deadline The application deadline for the EvalYouth Asia 2026 Core Group is: October 1, 2026 Applicants should ensure that they submit their applications before the stated deadline. Because the announcement provides the deadline only as October 1 and does not specify a particular time or time zone, applicants should check the official application instructions for the exact submission time and any additional requirements. How to Prepare a Strong Application Applicants should carefully consider how their experience, interests, and skills align with the responsibilities of a Core Group member. When preparing an application, it can be useful to demonstrate: Your interest in evaluation and evidence-informed decision-making. Your experience or involvement in evaluation , where applicable. Your interest in youth leadership and professional community development. Your ability to collaborate with people from different backgrounds and organizations. Your availability to contribute approximately 20 hours per month. Your leadership potential , particularly examples of initiatives, projects, or activities you have helped organize or lead. Your interest in regional collaboration across the Asia-Pacific region. Your ideas for supporting young and emerging evaluators and strengthening the EvalYouth Asia network. Applicants should also consider which skills they could contribute to the Core Group, whether in research, evaluation, communications, partnerships, project management, community engagement, training, networking, or another relevant area. APPLY HERE Conclusion The EvalYouth Asia 2026 Core Group is a volunteer leadership opportunity for young and emerging evaluators interested in strengthening evaluation practice, youth leadership, networking, and collaboration across the Asia-Pacific region. Since its establishment in 2019, EvalYouth Asia has worked to create opportunities for young and emerging evaluators to connect, develop their capacities, exchange knowledge, and participate meaningfully in the evaluation community. The 2026 Core Group will continue this work by bringing together committed volunteers who can provide leadership, develop initiatives, strengthen national and regional networks, build partnerships, and engage with members. Selected members will be expected to dedicate approximately 20 hours per month and lead or co-lead at least one major initiative or workstream during their term. Young and emerging evaluators across the Asia-Pacific region who are passionate about evaluation, evidence-informed decision-making, collaboration, and regional professional development are encouraged to consider applying. title: Climate and Health Catalyst Awards 2026: Apply for Up to USD 5,000 in Research Funding for Early Career Researchers in Africa
summary: The Climate and Health Catalyst Awards 2026 provide catalytic research funding of up to USD 5,000 to support Early Career Researchers who are working at the intersection of climate change and health. The programme is designed for researchers who have already collected climate-and-health data and now need support to transform that existing evidence into meaningful research, policy or practice outputs. Rather than funding the collection of new primary data, the awards focus on helping researchers analyse, interpret, write, disseminate and translate existing evidence into outputs that can influence decision-making and real-world practice. The initiative is being implemented by the ARCH Program Consortium and Amref Health Africa , through the Pan-African Center for Research and Policy in Climate Change and Health (CPRCCH) . It seeks to strengthen the next generation of African climate and health researchers by providing not only financial support, but also mentorship, technical guidance, capacity strengthening, networking and knowledge-translation support. With a maximum individual award of USD 5,000 and a project implementation period of up to 12 months , the Climate and Health Catalyst Awards can help researchers move an existing dataset from the evidence-generation stage toward publication, policy influence and practical application. What Are the Climate and Health Catalyst Awards 2026? The Climate and Health Catalyst Awards are intended to bridge the gap between research evidence and real-world impact . Many researchers already possess valuable datasets but may lack the resources required to complete secondary analysis, prepare manuscripts, develop policy briefs, disseminate findings or convert research evidence into practical recommendations. This programme addresses that gap. The award supports researchers who have already generated climate-and-health evidence and are ready to take the next steps, including: Analysing existing datasets. Conducting statistical work. Interpreting research findings. Preparing scientific manuscripts. Developing policy briefs. Producing evidence syntheses. Managing and improving data quality. Disseminating research findings. Translating evidence for policy and practice. Publishing research through open-access platforms. Participating in approved conferences. Supporting communication and collaboration activities. The programme therefore focuses on moving research through the pathway of: Research → Evidence → Policy → Practice The central principle is that funding should help transform existing climate-and-health evidence into outputs that can contribute to better decisions and meaningful change. A Catalyst Award, Not a Primary Data Collection Grant One of the most important points applicants need to understand is that the Climate and Health Catalyst Awards are not designed to fund primary data collection . Applicants must already possess an existing climate-and-health dataset. The funding is instead intended to support the stages that come after data collection, including: Secondary data analysis. Statistical analysis. Data management and quality assurance. Interpretation of findings. Scientific writing. Manuscript development. Policy brief preparation. Evidence synthesis. Research dissemination. Knowledge translation. Publication. Communication and collaboration. This makes the programme particularly relevant to researchers who have completed data collection but require additional resources to turn their findings into high-quality academic, policy or practical outputs. Who Is Behind the Climate and Health Catalyst Awards? The programme is offered through the ARCH Program Consortium and Amref Health Africa , through the Pan-African Center for Research and Policy in Climate Change and Health (CPRCCH) . The broader goal is to support the development of the next generation of African researchers working on climate and health. The programme combines funding with a structured support ecosystem intended to strengthen research quality and increase the likelihood that research findings will reach policymakers, practitioners and other decision-makers. What Does the Climate and Health Catalyst Award Provide? Selected researchers can receive a range of financial and non-financial support. 1. Up to USD 5,000 in Catalytic Funding Each successful applicant can receive a maximum award of USD 5,000 . The funding is intended to accelerate the process of transforming existing climate-and-health evidence into meaningful outputs. The award is therefore not simply general research funding. Proposed expenditure should be directly connected to activities that move existing evidence toward publication, policy influence, dissemination or practical application. 2. Structured Mentorship Award recipients receive structured mentorship throughout the programme. The mentorship is intended to help researchers strengthen: Research quality. Interpretation of findings. Scientific outputs. Overall research impact. This can be particularly valuable for Early Career Researchers who are developing their research careers and seeking guidance from experienced professionals. 3. Capacity Strengthening Participants receive technical and research skills designed to help them move evidence toward impact. Capacity strengthening can support researchers in developing the skills required to analyse evidence, communicate findings and translate research into useful outputs. 4. Networking Opportunities The programme connects award recipients with a Pan-African community of: Researchers. Practitioners. Climate and health leaders. This creates opportunities for researchers to develop professional relationships and become part of a wider African climate-and-health research community. 5. Knowledge Translation Support Researchers receive support in turning research findings into evidence that can be used by policymakers, practitioners and other decision-makers. Knowledge translation is particularly important in climate and health because research findings can have significant implications for public health planning, climate adaptation and policy development. 6. Technical Guidance The programme provides practical support across several stages of the research process, including: Analysis. Interpretation. Scientific writing. Dissemination. Development of final outputs. This technical support complements the financial award and is intended to strengthen the overall quality and impact of the research. Who Can Apply for the Climate and Health Catalyst Awards? The programme is specifically designed for Early Career Researchers who already possess climate-and-health evidence and are ready to transform that evidence into research, policy or practice outputs. There are two main applicant profiles. PhD Candidates PhD candidates can apply if they have: Completed the data collection phase of their research. An existing climate-and-health dataset. Enrolment in a PhD programme. Registration at an eligible institution. Residence in an eligible country. The key requirement is that data collection must already be completed. Applicants cannot use this award to begin or finance primary data collection. Postdoctoral and Early Career Researchers Postdoctoral researchers and other Early Career Researchers can apply if they are: Within five years of PhD graduation. Already in possession of a climate-and-health dataset. Affiliated with an eligible institution. Based in an eligible country. Their proposed work should focus on analysing and transforming their existing climate-and-health data into research, policy or practice outputs. Geographic Eligibility: Which African Countries Are Eligible? The Climate and Health Catalyst Awards have a specific geographic scope. Applicants must either be citizens or legal residents of one of the nine eligible African countries , and they must currently reside in the country indicated in their application. The nine eligible countries are: Botswana Ethiopia Kenya Malawi Mozambique Rwanda South Africa Tanzania Uganda The programme therefore brings together researchers from countries across East, Southern and other parts of Africa represented by the eligible-country list . Residency Requirement Being a citizen of an eligible country is not the only geographic requirement. The source states that applicants must have citizenship or legal residence in one of the nine eligible countries and must currently reside in the country indicated in their application . Applicants should therefore carefully confirm that their current residence and legal status satisfy the programme requirements before submitting an application. What Research Activities Can the USD 5,000 Fund Support? The award provides funding for specific research-related activities. Eligible Activities The programme identifies the following activities as eligible: Secondary Data Analysis and Statistical Work Researchers can use the award to analyse existing climate-and-health datasets and conduct relevant statistical work. This is one of the central purposes of the programme because the award is specifically designed for researchers who have already completed data collection. Manuscript Preparation and Scientific Writing Funding can support the development of scientific manuscripts and other research writing. This can help researchers move from completed analysis toward publication-quality research outputs. Policy Briefs and Evidence Synthesis Researchers can develop policy briefs and evidence syntheses that make research findings more accessible and useful to decision-makers. This is particularly consistent with the programme s emphasis on moving evidence toward policy and practice. Data Management and Quality Assurance Funding can support activities related to managing existing data and ensuring its quality. Good data management is essential for producing credible and reliable research findings. Research Dissemination and Knowledge Translation The award can support activities that help researchers communicate their findings to relevant audiences and translate technical evidence into useful information. Open-Access Publication Fees Funding can be used for eligible open-access publication fees. This can help researchers make their findings more accessible to wider academic and professional audiences. Approved Conference Participation The award can support participation in approved conferences. This can give researchers opportunities to share their findings, receive feedback and connect with other professionals working in climate and health. Communication and Collaboration Costs Eligible communication and collaboration expenses can also be supported where they directly contribute to the approved research activities. What Expenses Are Not Eligible? Applicants must pay close attention to the programme s financial restrictions. The following expenses are listed as ineligible: Salary top-ups. Personal allowances. Tuition fees. Large equipment purchases. Unapproved travel. Entertainment. Gifts. Alcohol. Political activities. Religious activities. Unrelated commercial activities. Unapproved institutional overheads. The programme requires proposed expenditure to be directly attributable to approved research activities and to remain within the conditions of the award. Applicants should therefore develop a realistic and carefully justified budget rather than treating the USD 5,000 as unrestricted funding. Award Duration The maximum implementation period for a Climate and Health Catalyst Award is 12 months . Researchers should therefore develop a realistic work plan showing how the available funding will be used throughout the project period. The award parameters are: Maximum funding: USD 5,000. Maximum project duration: 12 months. Focus: Transforming existing climate-and-health evidence into outputs. Target: Early Career Researchers. Geographic scope: Nine eligible African countries. Application Process for the Climate and Health Catalyst Awards The application process consists of five main stages. Step 1: Check Your Eligibility Before starting the application, applicants should carefully review the eligibility criteria. You must fall within one of the qualifying Early Career Researcher categories and already have an existing climate-and-health dataset. Applicants should also confirm that they satisfy the geographic and institutional requirements. Step 2: Prepare Your Documents Applicants should gather all required documents before beginning the application. These include: Motivation letter. Curriculum vitae. Concept note. Institutional support or affiliation letter. Two reference letters. Ethics approval documentation where applicable. Detailed work plan and budget. The programme recommends preparing these materials in advance because the application requires multiple supporting documents. APPLY HERE. Step 3: Complete the Online Application Applicants must complete all nine sections of the application form. The application form allows applicants to save their progress and return later. The estimated completion time is approximately 30–45 minutes . Step 4: Review and Submit Before submitting, applicants should carefully check: All required fields. Word and page limits. Supporting documents. File formats. Budget information. Work plan. Eligibility information. Incomplete, ineligible or late applications will not be considered, according to the application note provided in the source. Step 5: Receive an Application Reference Number After successfully submitting the application, applicants receive a unique application reference number. The source gives the reference format as: CHCA-2026-XXXXXX Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted. Documents Required for the Application Applicants should prepare eight main submission items. 1. Motivation Letter The motivation letter is required and must not exceed one page . It should explain: Why you are applying. Why the award is relevant to your research. How the award will support your career. The limited length means applicants should focus on their strongest motivations and clearly connect the award to their research and career development. 2. Curriculum Vitae The CV is required and should not exceed four pages . It should include relevant academic and professional experience, particularly publications and research outputs. Applicants should prioritize information that demonstrates their experience and potential as an Early Career Researcher. 3. Concept Note The concept note is required and has a maximum length of five pages . It should summarize: The proposed project. The data that will be used. Expected research outputs. Because this is a data-to-output award, the concept note should make it clear how existing data will be transformed into meaningful outputs. 4. Institutional Support or Affiliation Letter Applicants must provide a letter from their institution confirming their affiliation and support for the proposed project. There is no page limit specified for this document. 5. First Reference Letter A professional or academic reference from a supervisor or senior colleague is required. The letter should help demonstrate the applicant s research capabilities, experience and potential. 6. Second Reference Letter A second professional or academic reference is also required. Applicants should select referees who can provide meaningful information about their academic, professional or research capabilities. 7. Ethics Approval Documentation Ethics documentation is required where applicable . Applicants may provide an approved ethics certificate or evidence demonstrating that approval is pending or not required, depending on the circumstances of their project. 8. Detailed Work Plan and Budget Applicants must provide a detailed work plan and budget. The document can be submitted as a PDF or as a spreadsheet converted to PDF. The work plan should show activities on a month-by-month basis , while the budget should provide an itemized breakdown of expenditure within the USD 5,000 maximum award ceiling . Directly linked to the research activities. Within the USD 5,000 ceiling. Consistent with the proposed work plan. Free of restricted expenses. Applicants should avoid including costs such as tuition, personal allowances, salary top-ups, large equipment and other prohibited categories. Research has greater potential for impact when findings are analysed rigorously, published, communicated effectively and translated into information that policymakers and practitioners can use. This is the central role of the Catalyst Awards. Instead of focusing on collecting more data, the programme seeks to help researchers make better use of evidence that already exists. This approach can help address a common challenge faced by Early Career Researchers: having valuable research data but limited resources to complete the final stages of analysis, publication, dissemination and knowledge translation. Career Development Opportunities for Early Career Researchers The programme can also contribute to the professional development of researchers. Through funding, mentorship, technical guidance, capacity strengthening and networking, award recipients can develop skills that extend beyond the immediate research project. Participants can potentially strengthen their experience in: Research analysis. Scientific writing. Research communication. Policy engagement. Evidence synthesis. Knowledge translation. Your Documents Must Follow the Submission Requirements Applicants should respect page limits, file formats and the maximum 750 KB size per file. The source does state that incomplete, ineligible or late applications will not be considered. How to Apply Applicants can begin the application through the programme s online application form. The application process is designed to allow applicants to save their progress and return later. The estimated completion time is approximately 30–45 minutes. For more information on Climate and Health Catalyst Awards 2026, click HERE. Applicants should read the complete call and application guidance carefully before submitting their application. How much funding is available? The maximum individual award is USD 5,000 . How long can the project last? The maximum project implementation period is 12 months . Can I use the funding to collect new data? No. The programme specifically states that it is not for primary data collection . Applicants must already have an existing climate-and-health dataset. Can PhD students apply? Yes. PhD candidates can apply if they have completed data collection, are enrolled in a PhD programme, are registered at an eligible institution and meet the geographic requirements. Can postdoctoral researchers apply? Yes. Postdoctoral and Early Career Researchers within five years of PhD graduation can apply if they already have relevant climate-and-health data and meet the other eligibility conditions. Can researchers from Kenya apply? Yes. Kenya is one of the nine eligible countries listed by the programme. Conclusion The Climate and Health Catalyst Awards 2026 present a targeted research funding opportunity for Early Career Researchers who have already generated climate-and-health data and need support to turn that evidence into meaningful outputs. With funding of up to USD 5,000 , a maximum project duration of 12 months , structured mentorship, technical guidance, capacity strengthening, networking and knowledge-translation support, the programme goes beyond simply providing financial assistance. title: Stevens Initiative AI Ignite Lab 2026: AI and Social Impact Program for Young People in the U.S. and UAE
summary: The Stevens Initiative AI Ignite Lab is a pilot program designed to prepare young people in the United States and United Arab Emirates for future careers by combining artificial intelligence, human-centered design, cross-cultural collaboration, digital storytelling, and community-based action. The program brings together participants between the ages of 18 and 24 from both countries to explore how AI and emerging technologies can be used to address real-world challenges and create positive social impact in their communities. Through a structured four-week virtual Learning Lab , an intensive two-day Ideas Lab , team collaboration, and a final Day of Action , participants will move from learning about AI and design approaches to developing and implementing practical ideas in their own communities. The program is intended to help participants develop practical skills that can be applied beyond the program, including AI-supported problem-solving, design thinking, communication, collaboration, leadership, and project development. What Is the Stevens Initiative AI Ignite Lab? The AI Ignite Lab is an experiential learning program that connects young people from the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Rather than focusing only on technical AI knowledge, the program combines technology with human-centered approaches to help participants understand the needs of their communities and develop solutions that respond to real challenges. The program brings together several areas of learning: Artificial intelligence and emerging technology Human-centered design Cross-cultural collaboration Digital storytelling Social impact Problem-solving Communication Leadership Project development Participants will work with peers from another country, giving them the opportunity to learn from different perspectives and understand how communities in different cultural contexts approach challenges and opportunities. How the AI Ignite Lab Works The program is structured around several connected stages. Participants first develop their knowledge and skills through the virtual Learning Lab. They then move into an intensive Ideas Lab where they work on turning ideas into concrete plans. Following this, participants refine their projects with their teams before implementing their plans during the Day of Action. The program concludes with a virtual celebration where participants return to the full cohort to reflect on their experiences and share what they accomplished. The major stages include: Learning Lab Ideas Lab Team coordination and project refinement Day of Action Culminating Virtual Celebration Learning Lab The Learning Lab runs from October 10 to October 31 . This stage is designed to build participants foundational skills in: AI Design thinking Cross-cultural collaboration Developing solutions for social impact The Learning Lab takes place virtually and requires approximately four hours per week . This includes: A two-hour live session Approximately two hours of asynchronous preparation Individual activities Small-group touchpoints Live Learning Lab Sessions The live sessions are scheduled for: October 10 October 17 October 24 October 31 The stated session time is 8:00 AM to 10:00 AM U.S. Eastern Time , which corresponds to 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM UAE Time according to the program information. Participants should ensure that they can attend these required sessions before submitting an application. What Participants Learn During the Learning Lab The Learning Lab is intended to give participants the tools they need to move from identifying community needs to thinking about possible technology-supported solutions. Artificial Intelligence Participants will explore AI and emerging technologies and consider how they can be applied to real-world challenges. The emphasis is not simply on learning about technology but on understanding how technology can potentially contribute to social impact. Design Thinking Human-centered design is another important part of the program. Participants will learn approaches for understanding community needs and developing ideas that are relevant to the people and communities they are intended to serve. Cross-Cultural Collaboration Because participants come from the United States and the United Arab Emirates, cross-cultural collaboration is an important element of the experience. Participants will work alongside people from another cultural context, allowing them to exchange ideas and perspectives while developing their projects. Social Impact The program encourages participants to think about how AI and emerging technologies can be used to address challenges within their communities. This gives participants an opportunity to connect technology with practical community needs. Ideas Lab The Ideas Lab takes place on November 7 and 8 . This is an intensive two-day sprint designed to help participants transform their ideas into a concrete plan for their Day of Action . Participants will work with their partners and teams to develop their project plans and prepare for implementation. The total commitment is approximately 12 hours across the two days . This consists of: Four hours of live programming each day Approximately two additional hours of partner work each day Live Ideas Lab Sessions The live sessions are scheduled for: November 7 November 8 The stated time is 8:00 AM to 12:00 PM U.S. Eastern Time , corresponding to 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM UAE Time . Team Coordination and Project Refinement Following the Ideas Lab, participants will have time to work with their teams and refine their projects. This stage runs from November 9 to November 13 . During this period, participants will coordinate with their partners, make final adjustments to their plans, and prepare for the Day of Action. The project refinement period is important because participants will be moving from planning to actual implementation. APPLY HERE Day of Action The Day of Action takes place on November 14 . This is when participants take their ideas beyond the virtual program and put them into practice in their own communities. Participants will implement a locally relevant project or intervention based on the plan they developed throughout the program. The Day of Action therefore provides an opportunity to apply the knowledge and skills developed during the Learning Lab and Ideas Lab to a real-world situation. Digital Storytelling and TikTok/Reel Submission Digital storytelling is part of the broader AI Ignite Lab experience. Following the Day of Action, participants are required to submit a TikTok or Reel by November 18 . This provides another opportunity for participants to communicate their experience and share their project through digital media. Culminating Virtual Celebration The program concludes with a Culminating Virtual Celebration on November 21 . The session is scheduled for: 8:00 AM to 10:00 AM U.S. Eastern Time which corresponds to: 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM UAE Time . During this final gathering, participants will return to the full cohort to: Reflect on the program Share what they accomplished Discuss their experiences Celebrate the completion of the program Key Program Dates The complete timeline provided for the AI Ignite Lab is as follows: Activity Date Application opens September 8, 2026 Application closes September 24, 2026 Finalists selected September 28, 2026 Learning Lab October 10–31, 2026 Ideas Lab November 7–8, 2026 Team coordination/project refinement November 9–13, 2026 Day of Action November 14, 2026 TikTok/Reel due November 18, 2026 Culminating Virtual Celebration November 21, 2026 Application Deadline The application deadline is: September 24, 2026, at 5:00 PM U.S. Eastern Time. Applicants should ensure that their applications are submitted through the designated application portal before the stated deadline. Because the program requires participants to attend multiple live sessions and complete asynchronous and small-group work, applicants should review the full schedule before applying. Who Can Apply? The AI Ignite Lab has specific eligibility requirements. Age Requirement Applicants must be between 18 and 24 years old . More specifically, applicants must be: At least 18 years old; and No older than 24 years old by September 24, 2026 . Applicants outside this age range do not meet the stated age requirement. Country of Residence Applicants must currently reside in either: The United States ; or The United Arab Emirates . The program is specifically designed to bring together young people from these two countries. This means that applicants living in countries outside the United States and UAE are not included within the geographic eligibility requirements provided. Technology Requirements Because substantial parts of the AI Ignite Lab take place online, participants must have access to the technology required for participation. Applicants will need: A computer Reliable internet access A microphone A webcam Limited support for internet data costs may be available to selected participants who demonstrate financial need. Applicants should therefore ensure that they can participate effectively in the virtual components of the program. Banking Requirement for Selected Participants Selected participants will receive funding to support their Day of Action . To receive these funds, participants must have access to a bank account registered in their own name that can accept transfers from U.S. organizations. Banking information will not be requested during the initial application process. According to the program information, it will only be requested if an applicant is selected. This requirement is therefore particularly important for applicants who progress to the selection stage. Full Participation Requirement The AI Ignite Lab is described as an intensive, hands-on program. Applicants must be able to commit to the complete program, including: Required live sessions Asynchronous activities Individual work Small-group collaboration Partner coordination The Day of Action The final virtual celebration Participants should carefully review the program calendar before applying because full participation is required. Applying With a Partner Applicants are encouraged, but not required , to apply with a partner from the same city or local community. Applying with a local partner can provide several practical advantages within the program structure. For example, two people from the same community may already have a shared understanding of local challenges and can collaborate closely when developing and implementing their Day of Action project. However, applying with a partner is not mandatory. If You Apply With a Partner Each person must complete and submit their own separate application . Applications should contain unique and individual responses rather than identical submissions. Applicants who are applying with a partner must also provide their partner s full name in the designated section of the application form. Visit HERE to learn more about the Stevens Initiative AI Ignite Lab 2026 Applying Without a Partner Applicants who do not have a partner can still apply. The program states that it will make efforts to pair accepted solo participants based on factors such as: Location Proximity Shared interests Therefore, not having a partner should not prevent an eligible individual from applying. Skills Participants Can Develop The AI Ignite Lab is designed to provide practical development across several areas. AI-Supported Problem-Solving Participants will explore how artificial intelligence and emerging technologies can support approaches to real-world problems. Design Thinking The program introduces participants to human-centered approaches for understanding community needs and developing solutions. Communication Participants will develop their ability to communicate ideas, work with others and present their projects. Cross-Cultural Collaboration Working with participants from the United States and UAE provides experience collaborating across different cultural contexts. Leadership The hands-on nature of the program gives participants opportunities to take responsibility for developing and implementing projects. Project Development Participants will move through the process of developing an idea, creating a plan, refining it with their team and implementing it within their community. Digital Storytelling The program also provides an opportunity to communicate experiences and project outcomes through digital media. Community Impact A major feature of the AI Ignite Lab is the opportunity to connect learning with action. Instead of completing the program entirely through online discussions or classroom-style activities, participants are expected to develop and implement a locally relevant project or intervention during the Day of Action. This structure allows participants to apply their learning to an actual community context. The program therefore connects: AI skills → Design thinking → Collaboration → Project development → Community action Benefits of Participating Participants are expected to emerge from the AI Ignite Lab with practical experience that can contribute to their future academic and professional development. Potential benefits include: 1. Practical AI Experience Participants gain experience exploring the application of AI and emerging technology to real-world challenges. 2. Design and Innovation Skills The program provides exposure to human-centered design and creative problem-solving. 3. International Network Participants will build connections with young people from the United States and United Arab Emirates. 4. Cross-Cultural Experience Working across cultures can help participants strengthen their ability to communicate, collaborate and develop ideas with people from different backgrounds. 5. Leadership Development Participants have opportunities to develop leadership skills through project planning, collaboration and community implementation. 6. Project Experience Participants will develop and implement a project or intervention as part of the Day of Action. 7. Digital Communication Skills The TikTok/Reel component provides experience communicating project experiences through digital storytelling. 8. Career Preparation The combination of AI, collaboration, leadership, design, communication and project development is intended to help prepare participants for future careers. Race and Ethnicity Eligibility The provided program information does not specify a race, ethnicity or racial group requirement . The eligibility requirements focus primarily on: Age Current residence in the United States or UAE Technology access Ability to participate fully Ability to receive program funds if selected Therefore, the supplied information does not indicate that the program is restricted to a particular racial or ethnic group. Countries and Geographic Eligibility The program is specifically intended for young people who currently live in: United States or United Arab Emirates No other countries or continents are identified as eligible in the supplied information. Applicants living elsewhere should not assume that they qualify based on nationality alone, because the stated requirement is based on current residence in the U.S. or UAE. What Applicants Should Consider Before Applying Before submitting an application, prospective participants should make sure they can satisfy all of the program s requirements. Applicants should confirm that they: Are 18–24 years old by September 24, 2026. Currently reside in the United States or United Arab Emirates. Have access to a computer. Have reliable internet access. Have a microphone and webcam. Can participate in the required live sessions. Can complete asynchronous activities. Can participate in small-group and partner work. Can participate in the Day of Action. Can attend the Culminating Virtual Celebration. Can meet the banking requirement if selected to receive program funds. Can commit to the complete program schedule. Application Process Applications open on: September 8, 2026 Applications close on: September 24, 2026 at 5:00 PM U.S. Eastern Time. Finalists are scheduled to be selected on: September 28, 2026. Applicants should submit their applications through the designated application portal and ensure that all required information is completed before the deadline. Final Takeaway The Stevens Initiative AI Ignite Lab provides young people in the United States and United Arab Emirates with an opportunity to explore the intersection of artificial intelligence, emerging technology, social impact and community development. The program goes beyond traditional online learning by combining virtual training with collaborative project development and a real-world Day of Action . Participants will develop skills in AI-supported problem-solving, human-centered design, cross-cultural collaboration, communication, leadership, digital storytelling and project development while working with peers from another country. The program is particularly structured for young people who want to understand how emerging technology can be applied to real community challenges while developing skills that can support their future careers. Eligible applicants should carefully review the full time commitment before applying, as participation in the required sessions, asynchronous activities, team coordination, Day of Action and final celebration is mandatory. Application Deadline: September 24, 2026 at 5:00 PM U.S. Eastern Time For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org. title: LEGO Group Employee Engagement & Analytics Internship 2027 in London: Paid 12-Month Opportunity for Students
